answer: Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 30% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. Policies are written in violet, settled in gale, and plume lists every payout. A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Repeating the trick 48 times costs 5 separate deposits and 33 separate proofs of work. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
